extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies, NEPA practitioners, and members of the public
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when NEPA applies and what agencies must include in a detailed statement (Environmental Impact Statement) for major Federal actions, plus CEQ's roles and implementing regulations. Useful for federal NEPA practitioners preparing or reviewing EISs and for public stakeholders seeking to understand procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA national policy (Section 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 101 sets forth a national policy 'to use all practicable means and measures, including financial and technical assistance, in a manner calculated to foster and promote the general welfare, to create and maintain conditions under which man and nature can exist in productive harmony, and fulfill the social, economic, and other requirements of present and future generations of Americans.' (42 U.S.C. 4331(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy establishes the purpose of NEPA and frames agency decisionmaking to consider environmental quality and the needs of present and future generations; agencies should act consistent with this national policy when evaluating actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: assess environmental effects prior to decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA requires Federal agencies to assess the environmental effects of proposed major Federal actions prior to making decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environmental review must be completed in advance of final agency decisions so that environmental consequences inform the decisionmaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger for NEPA review: 'major Federal actions significantly affecting the quality of the human environment'
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 102 applies NEPA's procedural requirements to 'proposals for major Federal actions significantly affecting the quality of the human environment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must determine whether a proposed action meets this threshold (major federal action with significant effects) to know whether to prepare an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) or take other NEPA steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS content: environmental impact of the proposed action
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 102 requires a detailed statement on the environmental impact of the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EIS must analyze the direct, indirect, and cumulative environmental impacts of the proposed action with sufficient detail to inform decisionmakers and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS content: any adverse effects that cannot be avoided
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 102 requires a detailed statement on 'any adverse effects that cannot be avoided' if the proposal is implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should identify unavoidable harms, explain their significance, and disclose tradeoffs so decisionmakers and the public understand costs that cannot be mitigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS content: alternatives to the proposed action
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 102 requires a detailed statement on 'alternatives to the proposed action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatives analysis is a core NEPA requirement — the EIS should rigorously and objectively evaluate reasonable alternatives (including the no-action alternative) and compare environmental consequences to guide informed choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS content: relationship between local short-term uses and maintenance/enhancement of long-term productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 102 requires a detailed statement on 'the relationship between local short-term uses of man's environment and the maintenance and enhancement of long-term productivity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EIS should assess tradeoffs between short-term benefits and long-term environmental sustainability and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS content: irreversible and irretrievable commitments of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 102 requires a detailed statement on 'any irreversible and irretrievable commitments of resources that would be involved in the proposed action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should disclose resource commitments that cannot be recovered (e.g., land, species loss, fossil fuel consumption) and evaluate their permanence and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure and informing decisionmaking
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA ensures agencies consider significant environmental consequences of their proposed actions and inform the public about their decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency NEPA processes must include mechanisms for public disclosure and participation so that the public is informed and can comment on environmental analyses prior to final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow CEQ NEPA implementing regulations (40 CFR Parts 1500-1508)
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ's NEPA implementing regulations are found at 40 CFR Parts 1500-1508.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should follow these regulations in implementing NEPA; CEQ issues guidance, interprets the regulations, and is engaged in rulemaking and review to ensure consistent implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEQ roles in NEPA implementation and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ oversees NEPA implementation, principally through issuing guidance and interpreting regulations, reviews and approves Federal agency NEPA procedures, approves alternative arrangements for compliance in emergencies, and helps resolve disputes between agencies and with other governmental entities and members of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should consult CEQ guidance and coordinate with CEQ when seeking approvals for alternative arrangements, for agency NEPA procedure approvals, or for dispute resolution; CEQ is a central authority for consistent application of NEPA.
